summary.text: 还 is the simplified form of 還. Later forms of 還 are analyzed as 辵, a movement-related element, plus 瞏 as a sound element. The character is attested with the meaning “return”; modern 还 also means “still” and “yet.”

formation.text: Later forms of 還 have a phonosemantic construction: 辵 supplies the movement-related meaning, while 瞏 is identified as the sound element. A reported Old Chinese comparison is compatible with a sound cue, but does not independently verify the component analysis. A further proposal assigns 瞏 a meaning related to a round jade disc; the received analysis assigns it only a sound role. Reported early forms have different analyses, and their connection to the later construction is unclear.

components.text: In 还, 辶 is the conventional side form of 辵. 辵 is identified as movement-related in later forms of 還; this analysis does not apply to every reported early form.

不 is visible in modern 还, whose recorded structure is ⿺辶不. Its appearance does not establish a meaning or sound role in the older 還 construction. A separate dictionary entry records a 不-associated graph 还, but leaves its status unresolved and does not connect it to this variant.

In later forms of 還, 瞏 is identified as a sound element. A reported Old Chinese comparison between 睘 and 還 is compatible with that role, though it does not independently verify the component analysis. One analysis also proposes that 瞏 contributes a meaning associated with a round jade disc; the received analysis calls it phonetic.

sound_limitation.text: The comparison is reported, but the cited evidence does not independently establish 睘’s identity or reading as the phonetic component in 還.

sound.text: The reported Old Chinese forms share an initial and a final, with differences in vowel and medial details. This is a proposed sound comparison, not independent proof of the component analysis.

history.text: Reported oracle-bone forms of 還 are analyzed as 行/目/方; a separate Zhouyuan form is described as 彳/睘. Later bronze and seal forms are analyzed with 辵 and 睘. These accounts do not show a continuous change between the analyses.

The received dictionary analysis writes 還 as 从辵瞏聲. The form 还 is documented as a graphic variant of 還 and is used as its simplified form. A separate dictionary entry associates another graph 还 with 不 and other readings, but leaves its status unresolved and does not connect it to the modern variant.

uncertainties.text: The relationship between the reported early forms and the later 辵/瞏 construction remains unclear. The separate 不-associated graph 还 is not established as part of the modern variant’s history.
Although a Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison between 睘 and 還 is reported, the cited material does not independently verify 睘’s identity, reading, or phonetic role in 還.

senses.text: The received dictionary glosses 還 as 復, “return/repeat,” and classical citations record the sense “return.” Exact dates for the cited works and artifacts are not given.

senses.period: bronze and classical attestations; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: 還 is attested with the sense “go around” or “circle.” Its chronological relation to “return” is not established.
A classical citation uses 還 to mean “immediately.” Its relation to “return” or other senses is not established.

senses.period: Tang citations and later uses; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: Adverbial uses include “still” and “yet”; a Tang citation has the sense “still/again.” No dated chain connects these uses to “return.”

senses.period: later cited uses; exact chronology unresolved
senses.text: Cited uses include “also,” “more,” and “besides.” Their individual chronology and any path from “return” are not established.

limitations.text: The cited sources document several senses but do not establish a dated sequence or semantic bridges from “return” to “still,” “yet,” “also,” “more,” or “immediately.”

In cited manuscript passages, 還 is proposed as a sound-based spelling for 懷 and 環: a written sign was reused for other words thought to have sounded alike or similar. The cited material gives no pronunciation comparisons to demonstrate either match; these spellings do not show meanings developing from “return.”

overview.text: 还 is the simplified form of 還, whose attested meaning includes “return; go back.” Later 還 combines a movement-related element with a sound element. Modern 还 also means “still” and “yet.”

components.text: 辶 is the side form of 辵, identified as movement-related in later forms of 還.
不 appears in modern 还, but is not established as part of the older 還 construction.
The reported Old Chinese forms of 睘 and 還 resemble each other in their initial and final sounds, though this comparison alone does not prove 睘’s role.

takeaway.text: The visible 不 in 还 does not establish a sound role in the older 還 construction.

relationships.text: 辶 is the side form of 辵, identified as the movement-related component in later 還; 还 is documented as a graphic variant of 還.

The received analysis identifies 瞏 as the sound component in later forms of 還. A reported Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison is available, though the cited evidence does not independently verify the component’s identity, reading, or role.
还 is documented as a graphic variant of 還 and is used as its modern simplified form.
